title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the sequel to the Longue Marche, the previous page had begun 'Schémas en groupes associés aux extensions de groupes discrets'. The goal is to attach to a free Z-module of finite type M a pro-group scheme over S, indexed by the projective system of finite-index subgroups of M. The aim is presumably to linearize discrete or profinite extensions, such as fundamental-group extensions, into group schemes. This page sets up the general preliminary.

1. Start with an exact sequence of discrete groups (26) 1 -> M -> G -> H -> 1 with M commutative. H then acts on M by conjugation. The case of interest is M free of finite type over Z.

2. View M as a Z-module and define the functor underline-M : A |-> M (x)_Z A on commutative rings. This is the vector group (additive group scheme) attached to M, i.e. M (x) G_a, which is isomorphic to G_a^r when M = Z^r. For M free of finite type it is representable by a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over Spec Z.

3. Grothendieck wants Groups over S_0 (which seems to be Spec Z or a base over it): underline-G and underline-H, an exact sequence (27) 1 -> underline-M -> underline-G -> underline-H -> 1, and an isomorphism of exact sequences (28) recovering (26) on Z-points.

4. He takes underline-H = H_{S_0}, the constant group scheme with value H. Since Spec Z is connected, H_{S_0}(Z) = H. Likewise underline-M(Z) = M (x) Z = M.

5. Marginal note, written after the following page: one may simply set underline-G = G_{S_0} x^{M_{S_0}} underline-M. This is the contracted product, i.e. the pushout of the constant group-scheme extension 1 -> M_{S_0} -> G_{S_0} -> H_{S_0} -> 1 along the H-equivariant map M_{S_0} -> M (x) G_a. Concretely it is the quotient of G_{S_0} x underline-M by the antidiagonal M_{S_0}, with H acting on M (x) G_a through M.

6. The next page explains why. The naive functor A |-> (pushout of G along M -> M (x) A) is only a presheaf: it is correct when Spec A is connected and must be sheafified, i.e. 'localement constant' in the H-component. The pushout of constant group schemes performs exactly this sheafification.

Check on Z-points: underline-G(Z) is the pushout of G along M -> M (x) Z = M, which is G. So (28) holds.

Presumably one then replaces M by finite-index subgroups M' (pulling back the extension) to get the pro-system, with points over Z_l or Q giving partial completions of G.
errors: The claim that underline-M is representable, smooth and of finite type needs M free (or projective) of finite type. For M with torsion, A |-> M (x) A, e.g. A/nA, is not a smooth scheme, and indeed not representable. Grothendieck implicitly acknowledges this ('qui seront des schémas en groupes si M libre').
The transcription's 'schéma en groupes sur M' is surely 'sur Z' (Spec Z). It is a transcription slip, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Vector group scheme attached to a Z-module, A |-> M (x)_Z A
Group scheme extension of a constant group H by M (x) G_a, obtained by pushing out a discrete extension along M -> M (x) G_a (contracted product)
ideas.modern_name: pushout of extensions / 'algebraic hull' of a group extension with abelian kernel
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; related ideas in Malcev/Mostow algebraic hulls, and relative completion (Deligne, Hain)

ideas.what: The naive functor of extensions is only correct for connected Spec A and needs sheafification (locally constant H-component)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (constant group schemes), general topos formalism

ideas.what: Plan: a pro-group scheme over S indexed by finite-index subgroups of M, attached to extensions of discrete groups, in an anabelian/Galois context

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins a program to replace extensions of discrete (or fundamental) groups with abelian free kernel by pro-group schemes over Z: extensions of constant H by M (x) G_a, taken over finite-index sublattices. This apparently serves the extension/section criteria for homomorphisms into affine group schemes from the previous page. The page itself contains only routine preliminaries.
missed.quote: J'ai envie de définir aussi des Groupes sur S_0 ... underline-G, underline-H, et une suite exacte 1 -> underline-M -> underline-G -> underline-H -> 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginally relates to integral and l-adic versions of relative (unipotent) completion of fundamental groups, which the literature develops mainly over fields of characteristic 0. Whether the later pages carry this further is unknown from this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page (vector group of a lattice, pushout of a constant extension, sheafification remark) is standard. Only the intended use, linearizing discrete extensions into pro-group schemes over Spec Z within the anabelian program, is mildly interesting and is not developed here.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Généralités [?] préliminaire' reads 'Généralités préliminaires, relatif à une situation'.
'un schéma en groupes sur M [?]' should read 'sur Z' (Spec Z).
'Groupe constant de val. [?] H' should read 'Groupe constant de valeur H'.

The marginal note reads roughly 'J'ai vu en vérifiant que pour l'existence et construction de underline-G il suffit de poser underline-G = G_{S_0} x^{M_{S_0}} underline-M_{S_0}' (contracted product over the constant M_{S_0}). The isolated 'underline-M_{S_0}' is the superscript of that contracted product.

The duplicated phrase 'En tant que Z-module, et à ce titre [?] M est un Z-module' is a transcription doubling; the image reads 'En tant que tel M est un Z-module, et à ce titre définit un Groupe sur Spec Z'.
The equation label written '(17)' in the image corresponds to (27).
